title: message_send: one write path for thread, DM and channel messages

story.as_a: session that needs another session to know something
story.i_want_to: send one message to a work item, to a session or to a repo channel with one tool, and get the same stored message back if I retry
story.so_that: I never need to know which machine a session is on, and a retried send never duplicates or drops a message

rationale: PRD R11: a message is text, an author and exactly one attachment; it is stored before it is delivered, has an id, and a retried send is idempotent. Today the only write is channel_post (POST /api/v1/channel/posts, ChannelPostController.create/2, lib/loopctl_web/controllers/channel_post_controller.ex:892), which can address only a project; a DM to a session on another machine goes through claude-config's ssh courier bin/session-message.sh, and the keyless idempotency index channel_posts_idempotency_uidx is scoped by project_id, which a DM does not have. channel_post cannot simply grow two more targets: it also carries the handoff slot until release 7, and PRD R11 replaces free-text channel_post outright.

acceptance_criteria.description: POST /api/v1/messages (role: :agent, hierarchy) with body and exactly one of story_id, to_holder_id or project_id stores the message through Messages.send/4 and answers 201 {data: {id, story_id, to_holder_id, project_id, attachment_seq, author_holder_id, inserted_at}}; zero or two targets answer 422 code exactly_one_attachment.

Who may send: a channel or thread message passes Coordination.project_writable_by_agent/4 on the project (for a thread, the story's project); a DM needs a live or ended holder of the caller's tenant; a missing, foreign-tenant or non-member target answers the same byte-identical 422 code ownership_rejected, with no existence oracle.

The author is stamped from the verified key, never the body: agent_id from the key and author_holder_id from its holder_id (nil for a key with no holder); a key with no agent_id answers 403 code agent_identity_required.

A send carrying idempotency_key that the same agent already used in the tenant answers 200 {created: false} with the stored message and stores nothing, for every attachment kind: channel_posts_idempotency_uidx is rebuilt on (tenant_id, agent_id, idempotency_key) WHERE idempotency_key IS NOT NULL AND key IS NULL.
ChannelPost.create_changeset/2's bounds apply to every attachment kind: a body over 16 384 bytes, a NUL byte or a secret-denylist match answers 422 and stores nothing.

The MCP tool message_send takes body plus one of story_id, to_holder_id or project_id, generates an idempotency_key per call and reuses it on its own retry after a transport error, and its description names exactly_one_attachment, ownership_rejected and session_ended and says an agent key is needed.

Free-text channel_post is replaced: the MCP tool channel_post requires a key starting handoff: and refuses a keyless call before any request with a message naming message_send; POST /api/v1/channel/posts without a key still stores the body through Messages.send/4 as a channel message and answers its existing response shape, for MCP packages of the previous release (R7).

test_cases.name: send to each attachment kind; zero or two targets refused (ConnCase)
preconditions: human-anchored tenant; agent key that is a writable member of project; story in project; holder = fixture(:holder) (US-52.13)

test_cases.name: oracle-safe refusal for missing, foreign and non-member targets (ConnCase)
preconditions: tenant B with a project, story and holder; in tenant A a project where the caller has no assigned story; a random uuid
steps: send to tenant B's story, holder and project
send to the random uuid as story_id
expected_results: every response 422 ownership_rejected with byte-identical bodies

test_cases.name: author stamped from the key (ConnCase)
preconditions: a holder credential (US-52.13); a plain agent key; a user key with no agent_id
steps: send with each key, each body carrying author_holder_id and agent_id of someone else
expected_results: holder credential: author_holder_id = its holder; plain key: author_holder_id nil; the body's fields ignored; user key without agent: 403 agent_identity_required

test_cases.name: a retried send is idempotent for a DM too (DataCase)
steps: a send with k1 to a channel by another agent
expected_results: {:ok, m, :created}; {:ok, m, :deduplicated} with the same id and one row; the other agent's send creates its own row

test_cases.name: body bounds on a DM (DataCase)
expected_results: three {:error, %Ecto.Changeset{}} with a body error; no row

test_cases.name: message_send wiring, idempotency key reuse and description
preconditions: mcp-server with a stubbed fetch that fails the first call with ECONNRESET
expected_results: two POSTs to /api/v1/messages carrying the same idempotency_key; tool declared and dispatched (node --test); description contains exactly_one_attachment, ownership_rejected and session_ended

test_cases.name: keyless channel_post: refused by the tool, served by the route (node --test + ConnCase)
steps: call the MCP tool channel_post with no key
expected_results: the tool returns an error naming message_send and sends nothing; the route answers 201 in its old shape and the row has attachment_seq set and a 7-day expires_at

test_cases.name: tenant isolation of the stored message (DataCase)
preconditions: a message sent in tenant A

technical_notes: New route because none could serve: POST /api/v1/channel/posts (router.ex:255) is the channel-and-handoff write, whose request shape carries the handoff slot fields (key, session_id, supersedes, to_host, to_capability) that a message does not have, and it is deleted in release 7 with handoffs. POST /api/v1/messages and Messages.send/4 are the one message write; ChannelPostController.create/2's keyless branch calls Messages.send/4 (no second store, no second changeset).

Messages.send/4 (lib/loopctl/coordination/messages.ex): resolves the attachment, runs the gate, then Messages.insert/2 (US-52.22) inside one AdminRepo transaction with the audit entry (Audit.log_in_multi, action message_sent, entity channel_post). Returns {:ok, message, :created | :deduplicated} or {:error, reason}; 52.25 adds the ended-holder refusal to this function.

Gate: Coordination.project_writable_by_agent/4 (lib/loopctl/coordination.ex:900); project ownership via Projects.get_project/2 as in post/4 (:682-684); a DM's recipient via Loopctl.Holders.get_holder/2 (US-52.13) in the caller's tenant. Error mapping mirrors ChannelPostController render paths (:901-911 agent_identity_required, ownership_rejected).

Idempotency: today's index and its insert-and-recover (coordination.ex:598-612, channel_post.ex:326-329, migration 20260719150000_add_idempotency_key_to_channel_posts.exs); rebuild the index without project_id and update its Projects.Merge @unique_keys entry (lib/loopctl/projects/merge.ex:52-57) to columns agent_id idempotency_key.

MCP: tool declarations beside channel_post (mcp-server/index.js:4033) with a lib module mcp-server/lib/messages.js holding the request shape and the per-call uuid; handler case beside :10503; README rows for message_send; channel_post's description and the keyless refusal in the same module. The handoff tool (index.js:3960) keeps posting handoff: keys and is unchanged.

OpenAPI: operation/2 for MessageController.create with 201, 200 (deduplicated), 403 agent_identity_required, 409 session_ended (US-52.25), 422 exactly_one_attachment / ownership_rejected / changeset; CHANGELOG.md: new endpoint and the keyless channel_post change. Per-key caps are removed by US-52.26, so no controller rate plug here.
non_goals: Refusing a DM to an ended session and re-sending unread DMs: US-52.25.
Push delivery to subscribers and idle sessions: US-52.27.

failure_modes.partition: AC-52.23.4 and AC-52.23.6: a client cut off after the server stored the message retries with the same idempotency_key on reconnect and gets the stored message back, never a second one.
failure_modes.state: AC-52.23.1: the message is committed to channel_posts before the 201 is sent, so delivery (cursor reads) works from the stored row and a crash after commit loses nothing.
failure_modes.retry: AC-52.23.4: the rebuilt idempotency index dedupes a retried send of any attachment kind, DMs included.
failure_modes.slow: AC-52.23.6: the MCP tool retries a timed-out send with the same key, so a slow link makes delivery late and never duplicated.
failure_modes.reach: n/a: inline in the request process; the recipient is reached by attachment, never by machine (US-52.24 reads, US-52.27 wakes).

definition_of_done: From an MCP session on minis: message_send to a story id in another repo's project where the session is a member returns an id; SELECT story_id, attachment_seq FROM channel_posts WHERE id = <id> shows the story and seq 1 for a fresh thread.
defaults: A DM may be sent by any agent of the tenant to any holder of the tenant; there is no per-repo membership for DMs (owner may change).
